entries.title: Through the Gate
entries.body: I stepped through a moongate at sunset and woke at dawn beneath the spires of Britain. The air smelled of bread and rain. A man in a guard's tabard pointed me at the castle without a word.

entries.title: Iolo's Sheep
entries.body: Iolo asked me, with absolutely no irony, to recover his sheep. He claims they wander the Yew road on purpose, 'to spite him.' I have agreed to help, mostly because I am out of beer money.

entries.title: At the Shrine of Compassion
entries.body: I knelt before the stone and the wind dropped. I have read about this and never quite believed in it; the wind dropping was its own answer.

entries.title: Brigands at Despise
entries.body: We were three. They were nine. The Captain has been quiet ever since I returned without his men.

entries.title: The Codex of Ultimate Wisdom
entries.body: An old woman in the market said the Codex is real and not a metaphor. She was very sure. She was also missing several teeth and possibly drunk on cider, so I will note it but not yet believe it.
